detail: A read-every-line documentation audit found the published docs describing a product that no longer exists, plus two real code defects. Code: the CLI after-help advertised reproit capture and reproit list, neither of which is a command (both are under internal), so a first-time user failed and then re-read the same wrong advice in --help; and the Node backend package shipped files/exports that omitted instrument.js and replay.js, so a published tarball would have carried no capsule layer and require(pkg/instrument) would throw. Go: the module declared github.com/reproit/reproit-backend, a repository that does not exist, so go get 404d; renamed to github.com/ReproIt/reproit/sdk/reproit-backend-go across go.mod, the fiber submodule, every import, both example fixtures and the README, all building and testing green. Docs: five backend READMEs documented an event-batch-v1 wire format with backend and finding frames posted to /v1/events, which the code stopped emitting (all eight build one universal capture-batch-v1 for /v1/capture-batches with a hard one-operation assertion), so a reader configured the wrong endpoint and waited for a shape that never arrives; six claimed 16 operations per batch against that same assertion. The Rust SDK carried the last surviving tier block. docs/environment.md pointed all 64 of its file references at a src/ tree that does not exist (the root is crates/reproit/src/), verified now to resolve. docs/compatibility.md still carried the last sentence of the deleted CI-derived platform model. docs/cli.md claimed hermetic replay was Node-only. docs/self-dogfood.md instructed readers to cd into the private reproit-lab repo and used a check --runs flag that does not exist. Personal hostnames were removed from four published validation docs. No behavior changed beyond the two defect fixes; compatibility gate, 19 compatibility tests, 60 self-dogfood tests, SDK inventory, behavior coverage, Node SDK 25 tests, and the Go module and fiber submodule and both fixtures all pass, and fmt is clean.
